pulls.title: Preserve and validate telemetry provenance with durable delivery quarantine
pulls.body:
Smart Factory now preserves optional acquisition mode, run identity, measurement/receipt time, quality, connection and source events through MQTT persistence and retries. Its independently owned provenance validator rejects malformed metadata before persistence, normalizes real Gregorian UTC receipt timestamps, and keeps legacy unclassified input compatible.

Historical invalid records and receiver validation/credential/configuration failures enter durable quarantine without a false acknowledgement. Recoverable 404/408/409/429/5xx responses and unconfirmed timeouts retry the same ingestion identity with bounded backoff/Retry-After; redirects are disabled. The additive 20261026 migration retains bounded diagnostic codes and an explicit operator recovery path.

Revalidated on 2026-10-26 at fe86aca64aa09f6aca2efa6ad8ee9793f081ab5b: 207 tests passed, including 99 locally copied policy cases, permanent rejection, historical quarantine, timeout and successful recovery. [Backend CI passed](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-iot-backend/actions/runs/40246092902). A real Smart Factory edge/Mosquitto/.NET 8/authenticated Node path kept 20 simulated/replay samples durable during receiver outage, then acknowledged all 20 after recovery.

[Policy and recovery](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-iot-backend/blob/feat/equipment-telemetry-provenance/docs/telemetry-provenance-policy.md). No peer SDK/viewer/schema, mandatory Onesa service, physical-equipment qualification or external-consumer acceptance is introduced or claimed. Keep draft; no merge or manual production deployment.

[Final independent workspace qualification and repeated ingestion evidence](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-iot-frontend/blob/feat/native-equipment-monitoring/docs/equipment-evidence.md) records the exact tested sources, receiver outage/recovery and remaining physical/external qualification gates.

pulls.title: Qualify .NET 10 LTS with persisted authorization and scoped telemetry
pulls.body:
Operational service authorization now checks persisted dashboard sessions, current roles, disablement and revocation. Telemetry preserves canonical punctuated IDs, verified MQTT 5 retained context, source measurements/units and evidence modes through durable forwarding. Coverage applies scope and unit policy before aggregation. Runtime capability/schema/worker identities support coordinated frontend compatibility checks.

.NET 10 LTS is pinned across frameworks, compatible dependencies, SDK 10.0.403, runtime 10.0.14, combined ARM64 and standalone containers. All five standalone images build with the runtime's non-root app user.

Validation: 233 passing solution tests with real PostgreSQL policy fixtures; dependency audit; five CI image builds. The frontend qualification independently exercises actual BaSyx AASX/administrative metadata/semantic submodel/attachment import, provisioning and Pi profile publication, stub-only serial command/ack and role denial, both RabbitMQ and Mosquitto delivery, Node forwarding, duplicate/restart/outage/restore, notifications, scoped units/coverage, and six-service ARM64 compatible rollback/roll-forward.

Coordinated UI/evidence PR: DruHustle/smart-factory-iot-frontend#6. Gateway/firmware contract: DruHustle/smart-factory-iot-edge#4. Exact qualification sources and image are generated in the frontend evidence manifest. No production promotion, physical command, firmware flash or actual external consumer acceptance is claimed.

Delivery source: [43ad1f3](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-iot-backend/commit/43ad1f3153326424e97d1e1fd1844a86598e99b9).

pulls.title: Support legacy brokers through explicit historical-only MQTT intake
pulls.body:
The managed production broker rejected MQTT 5 (CONNACK 01) while accepting MQTT 3.1.1. Keep MQTT 5 as the default and reject automatic/ambiguous downgrades. A deliberate MqttProtocolVersion=3.1.1-historical mode restores intake while always marking telemetry and heartbeat transport flags unverified, so neither can update current state or threshold incidents.

239 solution tests pass, including six protocol-policy cases. Real disposable MQTT 3.1.1/.NET/Node/DB regression passed with zero current effects, plus retained delivery, duplicates, restart/outage and restore. The original MQTT 5 RabbitMQ path passed unchanged with its current-state and retain assertions. No broker ACL, credentials, paid service or hardware change is required.

The paired frontend qualification PR pins this source and adds the historical-mode path to CI. Production UI promotion is temporarily held until the corrected worker is independently subscribed and healthy.

pulls.title: Fit PostgreSQL pools and idle workers to the Free instance
pulls.body:
The shared application and BaSyx pool caps could request about 32 connections from the 20-slot Aiven Free instance. This change budgets 15 steady-state client connections and lets unused .NET connections expire sooner.

Telemetry outbox checks back off to 30 seconds when empty or unavailable. A coalesced wakeup after durable acquisition resumes delivery immediately for new samples. Notification polling also backs off when idle. Existing persistence, deduplication, retry deadlines and quarantine behavior remain in use.

Validation passed at 577288a9ce409e0d8465ae763169d9f30ceea638: all 243 backend tests, including both PostgreSQL integration tests, and all five standalone service image builds. NuGet restore passed high/critical dependency auditing with the pinned .NET 10.0.403 SDK. [Successful CI run](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-iot-backend/actions/runs/40572415187).

Application and BaSyx caps require a coordinated manual Oracle rollout. The runbook documents the 15-connection budget, live database memory policy, verification and rollback. The live Aiven memory safeguards were applied separately; this PR has not deployed the application candidate.

pulls.title: Deliver password reset links for approved individual accounts
pulls.body:
## Why
Approved users need self-service password recovery, and individual accounts must retain their assigned role when the same installation also offers shared demonstration logins.

## Changes
- Deliver the frontend's encrypted, one-time reset-link queue through the existing SMTP, Resend or SES sender. Validate current account status, authentication version, recipient policy, payload integrity and canonical origin before sending.
- Bound delivery claims, retries and provider timeouts; clear encrypted payloads after acceptance or invalidation and keep tokens/addresses out of error logs. Missing migrations and queue outages keep the worker alive with bounded, sanitized logging.
- Apply database-current permissions to approved individual accounts regardless of the shared-demo deployment flag. Shared identities, revoked/disabled sessions and temporary credentials remain restricted.
- Pass the matching reset origin and existing SMTP settings through supported Compose configuration.

## Validation
- Pinned .NET 10.0.403: full solution **287 tests passed, 0 failures, 0 skips**, including real PostgreSQL queue/session tests.
- Shared Node/C# encryption fixture, migration-wait recovery, concurrent claims and late-completion guards passed. Test senders recorded synthetic messages; no real emails were sent.
- Configuration parsing, deployment checks and `git diff --check` passed. [GitHub CI](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-backend/actions/runs/41172529795) passed the full solution and all five standalone service-image builds for `bc8a31ad9ac99b8cce6c631d4d22c0918aa0c8e0`.

## Coordinated rollout
Companion to [frontend PR #31](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-frontend/pull/31). Qualify this exact backend commit with the frontend source pin, apply additive migrations 0033/0034 through the API-first release, then run one updated mail worker. API and worker require the same `DASHBOARD_SERVICE_TOKEN` and canonical `PASSWORD_RESET_ORIGIN`; provider credentials remain worker-only. This PR does not deploy Oracle or promote Vercel.

pulls.title: Verify reset emails through the real authenticated SMTP sender
pulls.body:
## Why
Password recovery previously had cryptographic and queue-policy tests with a recording sender, so a green result did not prove that the actual SMTP adapter could send a reset message.

## Changes
Add a loopback-only SMTP capture server with authenticated STARTTLS and a pinned ephemeral certificate. Drive the actual PasswordResetDeliveryWorker and SmtpMailSender through delivery of the Node-generated encrypted fixture. Assert the message contains the correct recovery link, the queue records provider acceptance, the encrypted payload is cleared, and the message is not sent twice. The fixture restores the process-wide certificate callback and runs in a nonparallel collection.

## Validation
39 password-reset tests passed against disposable PostgreSQL, with no skipped tests. The production NotificationService and DashboardAccess components match deployed revision bc8a31ad9ac99b8cce6c631d4d22c0918aa0c8e0. This PR changes tests only and requires no production deployment.

This verifies application transport to a local test endpoint. Production-provider acceptance, mailbox receipt and the account owner's final sign-in remain distinct live checks. No real mailbox, password or production database was used.

pulls.title: Add industrial device connectivity, OPC UA FX and TSN evidence
pulls.body:
Industrial acquisition needs a versioned driver/tag configuration and typed observations that preserve the existing asset profiles, commissioned gateway identities and durable telemetry delivery.

## Changes

- Add strict independent configuration and observation contracts for OPC UA, Modbus TCP/RTU, MQTT and OPC UA FX, including typed tags, quality, discovery and TSN evidence.
- Add service-token-protected connectivity configuration and expiring probe endpoints to DeviceService.
- Publish retained industrial desired state on `/commands/connectivity`, preserving the legacy retained asset document on `/commands`; probes remain non-retained.
- Validate complete UADP field layouts, exact 64-bit decimal values, local credential references, protocol-specific sources, bounded configuration and observation sizes, and explicit applied-revision receipts.
- Persist the additive `ConnectivityJson` field through the existing MQTT subscriber and PostgreSQL outbox. Preserve legacy ingestion identities and quarantine invalid historical connectivity.
- Preserve UTF-8 byte budgets for Unicode configuration and telemetry, and document the contract and commissioning requirements.

## Validation

- Pinned .NET SDK 10.0.403; audited dependency restore succeeded.
- Full .NET suite: **356 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, including real disposable PostgreSQL tests.
- Regression coverage includes private route authorization, configuration/probe validation, retained-topic separation, typed values, Unicode limits, legacy ingestion hashes, deduplication, restart delivery and historical quarantine.
- The migration test applies the prior manifest, inserts a legacy row, applies the additive migration twice, and verifies legacy preservation plus typed persistence/reload.
- Cross-repository local qualification exercised real MQTT 5, the compiled DeviceService/TelemetryService, Node ingestion and PostgreSQL.
- During a measured **3.229-second** isolated broker interruption, three observations entered the edge SQLite queue. Each appeared exactly once in both PostgreSQL stores with its original acquisition timestamp. The queue drained, all five fixture connections resumed, and the existing singleton telemetry worker reconnected without restarting. The final checked backend queue had 560 distinct accepted/forwarded records, zero pending and zero quarantined.
- The published source tree exactly matches tested local commit `6f325c460a0e36fc6e3b56cfac93913ada45d706`: tree `3db93fbc0cf6ba64a8d9b8889346f84383f1a3be`.

## FX and TSN boundary

This is read-only acquisition and evidence transport. FX support covers model discovery and an explicitly commissioned unsecured scalar UADP observer. It does not establish FX control connections. TSN reports preserve local clock, interface, queue and collector evidence; both FX and TSN require `determinism: "unverified"`. Software fixtures do not certify physical controller, NIC, switch or timing conformance.

## Rollout

Apply `20261031_industrial_connectivity.sql` through the ordered telemetry migration manifest before starting the updated worker. Commission the gateway-specific broker permission for the additional retained topic. Coordinate the compatible dashboard and edge revisions and retain a single telemetry worker. This PR does not merge or deploy the services.

pulls.title: Separate Oracle backend display names from host identity
pulls.body:
## Why

The Oracle instance now hosts the Smart Factory API and singleton worker alongside the separate BaSyx stack. Its resource labels still describe only the former BaSyx role. The current `instance_name` setting also controls VNIC DNS and the guest hostname, so changing it to rename console labels would change more than intended.

## Changes

- Add display-only `instance_display_name` and `resource_name_prefix` settings, defaulting to `Software Engineering Backend` and `software-engineering-backend`.
- Update the seven instance/network `display_name` expressions.
- Preserve the legacy hostname, DNS labels, Terraform resource addresses, cloud-init, provider lock, IP settings, routes and security rules.
- Document the separate naming settings and how to keep the maintained variables consistent with OCI console labels without applying unrelated infrastructure drift.

## Verification

- `git diff --check` passed.
- Static comparison confirmed that all `main.tf` content outside the seven display-name expressions is unchanged; cloud-init, outputs, provider versions and lockfile are byte-identical.
- GitHub comparison confirms one commit and exactly four Terraform-module files changed from current `main`.
- Terraform is unavailable in the review environment, so `terraform fmt`, validation, plan and apply were not run.

## Operational scope

This draft is source maintenance only. No Terraform state or runtime deployment is included. Before any future apply, use the installation's existing state and variable file, retain its actual hostname, and require a plan containing only the intended display-name changes (or no changes). The module's latest-image lookup and complete network-rule configuration can otherwise introduce unrelated drift.

pulls.title: Make AAS compensation and notification delivery ownership safe
pulls.body:
Cancelled AAS provisioning could leave upstream writes behind, and a delayed notification worker could overwrite a newer delivery result. Compensation now uses an independent bounded cancellation token; delivery completion must match the processing state, attempt and lease. Regression cases cover both scenarios.

Docker contexts now exclude credential and generated paths, and deployment guidance reflects the existing Oracle API, singleton worker, Vercel and consolidated local tools. Previously reviewed OPC UA boundary and SMTP transport fixes are included.

Exact backend revision `e5634a58276dfacbc1e117db2f5a72b44b2228be` passed hosted checks and 364 reported tests against disposable PostgreSQL. Two optional methods returned early without live AAS or the vendor corpus. Real isolated services covered BaSyx, PostgreSQL, Redis and MQTT, with simulated serial acknowledgement, outage/restart, deduplication and database restore. Native ARM64 qualification passed with frontend `8a0a22a` and edge `1deb53c`, including candidate and fallback recovery and independent artifact inspection.

No application migration or production account change is included. Physical equipment, the external vendor corpus and mailbox delivery were not verified. Production has not yet been deployed.

pulls.title: Prepare Onesa domain, mail and private PostgreSQL candidate
pulls.body:
## Why
The requested move to factory.onesa.eu and the Onesa backend needs reviewed domain, mail and database configuration while retaining the current serving stack and external database primary.

## Changes

- Add deliberately incomplete API and singleton-worker environment examples using the implemented bundled runtime, canonical UI/reset origin and actual Resend variable names. Preserve existing signing, service, MQTT and database identities.
- Add an opt-in, separate PostgreSQL Compose project. Image digest/platform, postgres UID/GID, resource budgets, an existing durable volume, private bootstrap password file and existing TLS directory are required inputs.
- Require TLS/SCRAM for network sessions, reject plaintext and network login for the named postgres role, and keep the database on an internal network with no published ports.
- Add a network-only application overlay that preserves the API's existing networks and explicitly preserves the worker's otherwise implicit default network.
- Document restore, TLS, persistence, singleton-worker, backup and cutover qualification. Explain that HBA does not detect every restored superuser and that the current image runs startup migrations with the configured application connections.
- Add nine source/configuration checks to existing CI. Docker Compose is used only to render synthetic configuration and verify merge behavior; it does not start images or services.

## Review and validation
This is freshly authored preparation after the previous local environment became unavailable, not a byte-identical recovery of unpublished local commits. Independent review checked the actual application environment, mail and Compose contracts and found no remaining material source defect.

Fresh hosted [Backend quality checks run 41708989056](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-backend/actions/runs/41708989056) passed at commit 8315e63b77e5f8934105bc5b3941161844a9e40a (tree 11f9d4bfb638c6f27ebe2b7d0a3e1a0b5234fbfa). All six jobs succeeded, including the nine new source/actual-Compose configuration checks, existing .NET tests and NuGet audit, and standalone service image checks. This is fresh evidence for this tree; it does not qualify the optional database image's initialization, authenticated TLS, persistence or restore.

## Deployment status and remaining qualification
Source candidates only. No domain, mail provider, database primary, serving workload or infrastructure was changed. No image digest, actual DB UID, capacity or destination has been selected by these examples.

Before any rollout, qualify the selected image's non-root initialization and PostgreSQL data layout, an authenticated TLS connection with negative CA/hostname tests, a consistent restore, persistence across restart/recreation and private network isolation. Audit restored administrative roles, preserve the existing singleton MQTT client/session and durable backlog, and keep one active writer/primary. Real delivery and reset redemption must be tested before advertising email readiness. Retained data and compatible rollback images remain required. Kubernetes installation and workload conversion are separate qualification work.
